whoIsThisFor.heading: Who is the OmniStudio Consultant exam for?

personas.label: Hands-on practitioners
personas.description: You use OmniStudio and want to demonstrate how you apply its tools to implementation requirements.

personas.label: Consultants and admins

examDifficulty.heading: Is the OmniStudio Consultant Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: The exam asks you to translate Industry Cloud requirements into OmniStudio designs. Be ready to select between guided OmniScripts, contextual FlexCards, DataRaptors, and Integration Procedures, then reason about how the components exchange data.
bullets: 60 scored questions in 105 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
67% to pass, which is 41 correct answers out of 60.
Scenario-based choices: practice choosing between OmniScript, DataRaptor, and FlexCards.
Hands-on practice helps: configure OmniStudio features and review how they work together.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Build one end-to-end solution and inspect the JSON at each stage. You should be able to explain when an OmniScript calls a Data Mapper, when it calls an Integration Procedure, and what the caller receives.

examFormat.heading: OmniStudio Consultant Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: This proctored exam checks how you design OmniStudio solutions for real business processes. Use the 105-minute limit to work through the requirement, identify the component responsibilities, and trace the data flow.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Questions describe a user journey or data-processing task. Decide whether the solution needs a guided script, a data display, a data operation, or server-side orchestration.
bestWayToPass: Map the component roles: Match user input to OmniScript, a compact record view to FlexCard, data access to Data Mapper, and server-side orchestration to Integration Procedure.
Trace the JSON: Follow one value from an Extract through an OmniScript or procedure and into a Load or response.
Compare server-side choices: Know when a single Data Mapper is enough and when several calls belong in an Integration Procedure.
Debug a real build: Use preview output to find missing keys, incorrect mappings, and errors between components.

certificationCard.description: This exam covers solution design with OmniStudio: choosing FlexCards, OmniScripts, DataRaptors, and Integration Procedures for guided experiences and Industry Cloud implementations. The exam is 60 scored questions in 105 minutes, with a 67% pass mark, weighted towards Flexcards (18%) and Omniscripts (17%).

keyConcepts.h2: OmniStudio Consultant: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: FlexCards: Displaying Data Contextually
blocks.body: FlexCards show contextual data from Salesforce records or connected sources within Experience Cloud, Lightning pages, or other OmniStudio experiences. Child cards can surface related records. A custom action can launch an OmniScript, open a Lightning component, or navigate to a record. Data can come from a DataRaptor Extract, Integration Procedure, or Apex. Use a card to give users relevant details where they need them.

blocks.heading: OmniScripts: Guided User Experiences
blocks.body: OmniScripts guide a user through a multi-step process. Steps and groups organize inputs such as text, dates, selections, checkboxes, and lookups. Conditional display rules can reveal elements based on earlier responses; data sources can populate choices or prefill fields. Validation checks business rules before the user continues. Common uses include onboarding, service requests, and claims.

blocks.heading: Integration Procedures: Backend Orchestration
blocks.body: Integration Procedures coordinate backend work without requiring user interaction. OmniScripts and FlexCards can call them, as can other processes. An IP can query or write Salesforce data through DataRaptor actions, call an external REST service through HTTP Action, invoke Apex, set values, and branch or loop. It can combine and transform results from multiple sources before returning them to the caller.

blocks.heading: DataRaptors: Data Access and Transformation
blocks.body: DataRaptors handle reading, writing, or reshaping data. Extract reads Salesforce data into structured JSON; Load creates or updates records; Transform maps between structures without writing to Salesforce; Turbo Extract performs a simpler, optimized read using SOQL. Choose the type to match the operation. A Load can create related parent and child records in one operation.

blocks.heading: OmniStudio Architecture in Industry Clouds
blocks.body: Industry Clouds include Health, Financial Services, Communications, and Energy and Utilities. Their packages can provide industry-specific OmniScripts and FlexCards, which teams configure or extend. These components work with standard Salesforce objects and industry data models. Business Rules Engine offers declarative if-then logic that can guide OmniScript branches without hard-coding those decisions.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce OmniStudio Consultant Exam
scenarioTips.intro: Start with the business requirement, then choose the OmniStudio components and data flow that fit it.

blocks.heading: Tool Selection Framework
blocks.body: Match each task to its tool. FlexCards display contextual information, OmniScripts guide users through steps, DataRaptors handle Salesforce data, and Integration Procedures coordinate server-side work.

blocks.heading: Business Process to OmniScript Mapping
blocks.body: Break the business process into guided steps and map the data each step needs. Consider a sub-OmniScript when the same process can be reused.

blocks.heading: Data Integration Architecture
blocks.body: Compare DataRaptor Extract with an Integration Procedure when retrieving data. Review transformation needs and whether the procedure must call an external API.

blocks.heading: FlexCard Use Cases
blocks.body: Use FlexCards to present information such as account details or case summaries. Plan states for loading, empty, error, and populated results.

blocks.heading: Performance & Scalability
blocks.body: Review performance by reducing unnecessary DataRaptor steps and server calls. Consider Turbo Extract for simple reads and caching when Integration Procedure results can be reused.

sampleQuestions.question: What does an OmniStudio Consultant mainly do?
options: Configure CPQ price rules and product bundles for the sales operations team
Design and build sustainable, scalable OmniStudio solutions that meet business needs
Build email campaigns in Marketing Cloud
sampleQuestions.explanation: An OmniStudio Consultant designs and implements solutions with OmniStudio tools to meet business needs and support long-term success.
whyWrong: CPQ is not the only focus of the role.
Slack is not the only focus of the role.
Email is not the only focus of the role.

sampleQuestions.question: Which OmniStudio tool creates guided, step-by-step experiences?
sampleQuestions.explanation: OmniScript guides users through a sequence of steps, fields, and actions.
whyWrong: DataRaptor handles data extraction and transformation.
FlexCards display record information in a card format.
Integration Procedures handle server-side data and service operations.

sampleQuestions.question: What should a consultant consider when designing for long-term success?
options: A design built for a single use case
sampleQuestions.explanation: A good design should meet current needs and be sustainable, scalable, and useful to the customer over time.
whyWrong: A design that works only once may not meet future needs.
Documentation helps teams maintain the solution.
Speed alone does not guarantee a reliable solution.

sampleQuestions.question: Which set of industries commonly uses OmniStudio solutions?
options: Manufacturing companies and no other industries
Retail and consumer goods companies exclusively
Schools and universities, but not commercial businesses
Financial Services, Insurance, and other industries
sampleQuestions.explanation: Financial Services and Insurance are examples of the industries that use OmniStudio, whose configurable components support industry-specific workflows.
whyWrong: OmniStudio is not limited to Manufacturing.
OmniStudio is not limited to Retail.
OmniStudio is not limited to Education.

sampleQuestions.question: What kind of information does a FlexCard present to a user?
options: A library of reusable email templates
A compact card view of record data
sampleQuestions.explanation: FlexCards display data in a compact, card-based format.
whyWrong: Slack messages are not the purpose of FlexCards.
Email templates are not the purpose of FlexCards.
FlexCards are not limited to reports.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a DataRaptor do in OmniStudio?
options: Creates reports and dashboards for managers
sampleQuestions.explanation: DataRaptors extract, load, and transform data for OmniStudio solutions.
whyWrong: DataRaptors work with data; they are not limited to creating reports.
Sending email is not their main purpose.
Managing users is not their purpose.

sampleQuestions.question: Which OmniStudio component can call Apex or external services?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Integration Procedures can orchestrate calls to Apex, DataRaptors, and external services.
whyWrong: OmniScripts guide users and can call other components, but they are not the component described.
FlexCards display data and actions, but they are not the component described.
DataRaptors handle data operations, but they are not the component described.

sampleQuestions.question: What types of checks can OmniScript validation support?
options: Required fields, with no other kind of check available
No validation; checks must be written in Apex
Required fields, custom validation, and conditional rules
Custom validation rules, but not required fields
sampleQuestions.explanation: OmniScript can check required fields, run custom validation, and apply conditional rules.
whyWrong: Validation supports more than required fields.
OmniScript supports validation.
Validation supports more than custom rules.

sampleQuestions.question: A team needs a repeatable release process for OmniStudio assets between environments. Which deployment path should it use?
options: Copy the components by hand into each environment
Use standard change sets for every OmniStudio asset
Use OmniStudio FlexDeploy or source-driven deployment
No deployment method is available for OmniStudio components
sampleQuestions.explanation: FlexDeploy and source-driven deployment are supported ways to promote OmniStudio assets through a controlled release process.
whyWrong: Manual copying is not the only deployment option.
Change sets are not the only deployment option.
OmniStudio components can be deployed.

sampleQuestions.question: What do OmniScript elements define?
options: DataRaptor field mappings for an Integration Procedure
Steps, fields, and actions in an OmniScript flow
sampleQuestions.explanation: OmniScript elements define the steps, fields, and actions users see in the flow.
whyWrong: Elements do more than create FlexCards.
Elements do not only send email.
Elements do not replace DataRaptors.

sampleQuestions.question: How can OmniStudio show content or choose a path based on data or user input?
sampleQuestions.explanation: OmniStudio supports conditional visibility and branching based on data or user input.
whyWrong: The available logic is not limited to visibility.
The available logic is not limited to branching.
OmniStudio supports conditional logic.

sampleQuestions.question: What helps an OmniStudio solution scale?
options: Build every flow for one use case and copy it whenever a similar need appears
Reusable components, efficient DataRaptors, and good governance
sampleQuestions.explanation: Reusable components, efficient DataRaptors, and governance can improve performance and maintainability as a solution grows.
whyWrong: Performance matters as usage grows.
Reuse helps teams maintain and extend solutions.
Designing only for one use can make future changes harder.

sampleQuestions.question: Which OmniStudio components can be placed on Lightning pages?
sampleQuestions.explanation: OmniScripts and FlexCards can be embedded in Lightning pages.
whyWrong: Some OmniStudio components can be placed on Lightning pages.
DataRaptors are data tools, not page components.
Integration Procedures run server-side and are not page components.

sampleQuestions.question: What is one benefit of OmniScript compared with building a custom Apex user interface?
options: More complexity, because every step has to be coded and tested by a developer
A guided flow can be quicker to build and easier to maintain declaratively
sampleQuestions.explanation: OmniScript offers a declarative way to build guided flows, which can take less effort to maintain than a custom Apex interface.
whyWrong: OmniScript can offer benefits for guided flows.
A custom Apex interface can require more code and maintenance.
OmniScript is flexible for guided flows.

sampleQuestions.question: Which is a common OmniStudio use case in Financial Services?
options: Student course enrolment and grading for universities
sampleQuestions.explanation: OmniStudio can support Financial Services workflows such as quote-to-cash, customer onboarding, and service.
whyWrong: OmniStudio is used in more than Manufacturing.
OmniStudio is used in more than Education.
OmniStudio is used in more than Retail.

sampleQuestions.question: A client needs to read a large volume of Salesforce records quickly for a read-only lookup, with no transformation required. Which DataRaptor type fits best?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Turbo Extract is optimized for fast, straightforward reads of Salesforce data, ideal for simple lookups without complex transformation.
whyWrong: Load writes data into Salesforce, it doesn't read for a lookup.
Transform reshapes JSON data rather than extracting from Salesforce records directly.
A custom Apex class bypasses the declarative tool built for exactly this purpose.

sampleQuestions.question: Two independent data lookups are needed before an OmniScript can proceed, and neither depends on the other's result. How should the Integration Procedure be designed to minimize wait time?
options: Run the two actions in parallel within the Integration Procedure
Always run every action one after another, regardless of dependency
Split them into two separate OmniScripts
Avoid Integration Procedures entirely for this case
sampleQuestions.explanation: When actions don't depend on each other's output, running them in parallel inside the Integration Procedure reduces total wait time compared to sequential execution.
whyWrong: Running everything sequentially by default wastes time when actions are independent.
Splitting into two OmniScripts adds unnecessary complexity for what one Integration Procedure can handle.
Integration Procedures are exactly the right tool for this kind of data orchestration.

sampleQuestions.question: A consultant is deciding between building a new OmniStudio component from scratch and reusing an existing Integration Procedure that already does most of what's needed. What's the best-fit approach?
options: Favor reuse of the existing component over duplicating the logic
Always build a brand-new component, regardless of what already exists
Ignore existing components without reviewing them
sampleQuestions.explanation: Reuse over rebuild is a core OmniStudio best-fit design principle: a shared Integration Procedure called by multiple OmniScripts reduces duplicated logic and maintenance overhead.
whyWrong: Always building new ignores available reusable components and increases maintenance burden.
Avoiding reuse entirely contradicts a core OmniStudio design best practice.
Not reviewing what already exists risks duplicating logic unnecessarily.

sampleQuestions.question: A client wants a self-service quoting tool that walks the customer through several screens, collecting information at each step before submitting. Which OmniStudio component is the best fit?
sampleQuestions.explanation: OmniScript is purpose-built for multi-step, guided user experiences like a self-service quoting flow.
whyWrong: A FlexCard displays contextual information, it isn't designed for a multi-step guided interaction on its own.
A DataRaptor reads/writes/transforms data, it doesn't provide the step-by-step UI.
An Apex trigger runs on record changes in the backend, it doesn't provide a guided front-end experience.

sampleQuestions.question: A team updates an OmniScript already in production and wants to roll out the change without breaking the currently running version for users mid-process. What's the standard approach?
options: Create and activate a new version, rather than overwriting the active version directly
Edit the active version in place
Delete the component and rebuild it
Make the change in a sandbox, test it there, and never promote it to the production org
sampleQuestions.explanation: OmniStudio components support versioning; the standard approach is to activate a new version rather than editing the currently active one directly.
whyWrong: Editing the active version in place risks disrupting users currently in that flow.
Deleting and rebuilding loses configuration history unnecessarily.
A change that never gets promoted to production doesn't deliver the update to real users.
